pt.what-is-ai: As definições originais do curso: autonomia é "a capacidade de executar tarefas em ambientes complexos sem orientação constante de quem usa"; adaptatividade é "a capacidade de melhorar o desempenho aprendendo com a experiência" (tradução minha).
pt.bias: Os detalhes que o texto deixa de fora estão nas fontes. Dermatologia: queda de 27% a 36% no desempenho (Daneshjou *et al.*, 2022). Classificação de gênero: até 34,7% de erro para mulheres de pele escura e no máximo 0,8% para homens de pele clara, calculados a partir das acurácias publicadas (Buolamwini; Gebru, 2018). Reconhecimento facial: falsos positivos de 10 a 100 vezes maiores (NIST, 2019). A prisão é a de Robert Williams, em Detroit (ACLU, 2024). O sistema de alerta precoce é o do estado de Wisconsin, com 42 pontos percentuais de diferença no alarme falso (Feathers, 2023). O erro de tradução ocorreu no Facebook (Hern, 2017).
pt.data-privacy: O aplicativo citado é o Ever; a autoridade é a Federal Trade Commission, dos Estados Unidos.
pt.footprint: Os valores por trás das ordens de grandeza do texto: 0,24 Wh e 0,26 ml por prompt de texto mediano (Vahdat; Dean, 2025); 0,34 Wh por consulta média (Altman, 2025); cerca de 3,4 milhões de joules para cinco segundos de vídeo, mais de 700 vezes uma imagem (O'Donnell; Crownhart, 2025); 415 TWh consumidos por data centers em 2024, perto de 1,5% da eletricidade mundial, com projeção de cerca de 945 TWh em 2030 (International Energy Agency, 2025).
pt.context: A frase sobre CPU e memória é uma paráfrase do trecho em que Karpathy compara LLMs a um sistema operacional. De Anthropic (2025) vêm "orçamento de atenção", a "altitude certa" e o princípio do menor conjunto de tokens de alto sinal. A medição do *context rot* é de Chroma (2025).
pt.workspace: O fornecedor que criou limites semanais é a Anthropic (Zeff, 2025). Os números de uso deste capítulo são da minha própria rotina: em novembro de 2026, as três assinaturas somavam cerca de R$ 2.000 por mês, com o salário mínimo em R$ 1.621.
pt.agents-leash: A lista de riscos é a da OWASP; a "trifeta letal" é de Simon Willison (2025). O desenho do canal de suporte (quem pede, quem aprova) descreve um agente em produção na empresa em que trabalho.
pt.cases: Os oito casos são da minha rotina de trabalho e de aula; nomes de pessoas, clientes e empresas foram omitidos. A mudança de legislação do caso 1 é a reforma tributária brasileira. Sobre participantes sintéticos, as autoras escrevem: "Synthetic users cannot replace the depth and empathy gained from studying and speaking with real people" e "They often provide shallow or overly favorable feedback" (Rosala; Moran, 2024). Hugo Alves é cofundador de uma empresa que vende pesquisa com participantes sintéticos; na entrevista ele diz: "research is always about making better decisions [...] It's about reducing risk" (minuto 4); que não espera que alguém tome, só com isso, "a decision that can make a company break", e que é preciso achar "what should be left exclusively for humans" (minuto 17); e que quem muda de ideia costuma dizer "I wouldn't replace humans with this but now I really see where this could help me" (minuto 52).
pt.generalist: A fonte é uma entrevista de Karim R. Lakhani, professor da Harvard Business School. Trechos usados: custo marginal da expertise (minutos 34 e 47), os três jeitos de trabalhar com IA (2 a 4; na entrevista, cerca de 60% de ciborgues, 14% de centauros e 27% de autoautomatizadores), "nunca aceito a primeira resposta" (9), responsabilidade e "interface de carne" (3 e 14), o curso obrigatório do MBA, com cerca de 900 estudantes (20 a 22), e quem corre mais risco (44 e 45). Traduções e paráfrases são minhas. O experimento com profissionais de consultoria é o de Dell'Acqua *et al.* (2023).
pt._index: Lia é uma personagem inventada. Os dados do problema que ela enfrenta são reais: em 2025, 7,7 milhões de jovens de 14 a 29 anos não tinham concluído o ensino médio, e 43% apontaram a necessidade de trabalhar (IBGE, 2026); a Busca Ativa Escolar ajudou mais de 300 mil crianças e adolescentes a voltar à escola entre 2017 e 2025 (UNICEF, 2025).
pt.computational-thinking: Os trechos usados na seção de pesquisa, no original. Brennan e Resnick (2012): conceitos "sequences, loops, parallelism, events, conditionals, operators, and data"; práticas "being incremental and iterative, testing and debugging, reusing and remixing, and abstracting and modularizing". Denny *et al.* (2023, seção 4; versão final publicada em *Communications of the ACM*, 2024): "Without the skills to read, test and verify that code does what is intended, users risk becoming mere consumers of the generated content". Prather *et al.* (2024, resumo): estudo com 21 estudantes; quem teve dificuldade "thought they performed better than they did, and finished with an illusion of competence". Sarkar *et al.* (2022): "End-user programmers often lack computational thinking skills [...], such as the ability to decompose problems into subproblems [...]. However, effective use of LLMs such as Codex requires such skills."
pt.app-builders: A frase citada é contada por Guillermo Rauch, que a atribui a uma pessoa usuária da ferramenta dele (minutos 0 e 43 da entrevista): "v0 is a super genius five-year-old PhD with ADHD". Ela descreve aquela ferramenta, não a IA em geral; a generalização é minha. Os casos do capítulo são da minha rotina de trabalho; nomes de pessoas, clientes e empresas foram omitidos.

en.what-is-ai: The course's original definitions: autonomy is "the ability to perform tasks in complex environments without constant guidance by a user"; adaptivity is "the ability to improve performance by learning from experience."
en.bias: The details the text leaves out are in the sources. Dermatology: a 27% to 36% drop in performance (Daneshjou et al., 2022). Gender classification: up to 34.7% error for darker-skinned women and at most 0.8% for lighter-skinned men, computed from the accuracies published (Buolamwini & Gebru, 2018). Face recognition: false positives 10 to 100 times higher (NIST, 2019). The arrest is that of Robert Williams, in Detroit (ACLU, 2024). The early-warning system is the state of Wisconsin's, with a 42-percentage-point gap in false alarms (Feathers, 2023). The translation error happened on Facebook (Hern, 2017).
en.data-privacy: The app mentioned is Ever; the authority is the U.S. Federal Trade Commission.
en.footprint: The values behind the orders of magnitude in the text: 0.24 Wh and 0.26 ml per median text prompt (Vahdat & Dean, 2025); 0.34 Wh per average query (Altman, 2025); about 3.4 million joules for five seconds of video, more than 700 times one image (O'Donnell & Crownhart, 2025); 415 TWh consumed by data centers in 2024, close to 1.5% of the world's electricity, with a projection of about 945 TWh in 2030 (International Energy Agency, 2025).
en.context: The CPU-and-memory line paraphrases the passage where Karpathy compares LLMs to an operating system. Anthropic (2025) is the source for "attention budget", the "right altitude", and the principle of the smallest set of high-signal tokens. The context rot measurement is from Chroma (2025).
en.workspace: The vendor that introduced weekly limits is Anthropic (Zeff, 2025). The usage numbers in this chapter come from my own routine: in November 2026, the three subscriptions added up to about R$ 2,000 a month, with Brazil's monthly minimum wage at R$ 1,621.
en.agents-leash: The risk list is OWASP's; the "lethal trifecta" is Simon Willison's (2025). The support-channel design (who asks, who approves) describes an agent in production at the company where I work.
en.cases: The eight cases come from my work and teaching routine; names of people, clients and companies were left out. The change in legislation in case 1 is Brazil's tax reform. On synthetic participants, the authors write: "Synthetic users cannot replace the depth and empathy gained from studying and speaking with real people" and "They often provide shallow or overly favorable feedback" (Rosala & Moran, 2024). Hugo Alves is the co-founder of a company that sells research with synthetic participants; in the interview he says: "research is always about making better decisions [...] It's about reducing risk" (minute 4); that he does not expect anyone to make, on this alone, "a decision that can make a company break", and that one has to find "what should be left exclusively for humans" (minute 17); and that people who change their mind usually say "I wouldn't replace humans with this but now I really see where this could help me" (minute 52).
en.generalist: The source is an interview with Karim R. Lakhani, a professor at Harvard Business School. Passages used: marginal cost of expertise (minutes 34 and 47), the three ways of working with AI (2 to 4; in the interview, about 60% cyborgs, 14% centaurs and 27% self-automators), "I never take the first answer" (9), accountability and the "meat interface" (3 and 14), the required MBA course, with about 900 students (20 to 22), and who is most at risk (44 and 45). The experiment with consultants is Dell'Acqua et al. (2023).
en._index: Lia is an invented character. The data about the problem she faces are real: in 2025, 7.7 million people aged 14 to 29 in Brazil had not finished high school, and 43% pointed to the need to work (IBGE, 2026); Busca Ativa Escolar helped more than 300 thousand children and adolescents return to school between 2017 and 2025 (UNICEF, 2025).
en.computational-thinking: The passages used in the research section. Brennan and Resnick (2012): concepts "sequences, loops, parallelism, events, conditionals, operators, and data"; practices "being incremental and iterative, testing and debugging, reusing and remixing, and abstracting and modularizing". Denny et al. (2023, section 4; final version published in *Communications of the ACM*, 2024): "Without the skills to read, test and verify that code does what is intended, users risk becoming mere consumers of the generated content". Prather et al. (2024, abstract): a study with 21 students; those who struggled "thought they performed better than they did, and finished with an illusion of competence". Sarkar et al. (2022): "End-user programmers often lack computational thinking skills [...], such as the ability to decompose problems into subproblems [...]. However, effective use of LLMs such as Codex requires such skills."
en.app-builders: The quoted line is told by Guillermo Rauch, who attributes it to a user of his tool (minutes 0 and 43 of the interview): "v0 is a super genius five-year-old PhD with ADHD". It describes that tool, not AI in general; the generalization is mine. The cases in the chapter come from my own work; names of people, clients and companies were left out.
